- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥ 0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per subsequent period to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model underestimates downside; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated bearish signals (≥ 3 consecutive 0.00–0.33), apply mean reversion rule: forecast = prior 5-day average + 0.5% decay.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is consistently below true outcome by >5% over 3+ consecutive periods, shift forecast baseline up by 1–2% to align with recent trend.  
- If official events include multiple auctions in same period, model tends to overestimate supply impact; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per auction event.
